problem:
Determine whether ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14041802/assets/59af73d1cda1a988c775ccf198b53653b96660b4ad8416add1b0c1816e89a5a5.png) is an eigenvector of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14041802/assets/963bcaf94bc481fe8fbc99ca28fba037047d8821661eadcf0e5e9ce50ba39ef8.png)
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $\mathbf{v}$ such that $A\mathbf{v}=\lambda \mathbf{v}.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 8 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1+3\text{i} \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18+6\text{i} \\ 24\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18{\text{i}}^{2}+6\text{i} \\ 24\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =6\text{i}[\begin{aligned}1+3\text{i} \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =6\text{i}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $A\mathbf{v} = 6\textrm{i} \mathbf{v},$ we conclude that $\mathbf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda=6\textrm{i}.$
